newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy calls June 18 conference on Albania.
newsitem.headline: Italy calls June 18 conference on Albania.

text.p: Italy said on Wednesday it planned to host an international conference on Albania on June 18 in Rome to study political, economic and financial matters with the aim of contributing to the stabilisation of the Balkan country.
The Foreign Ministry said in a statement that the conference, which will be at ministerial level, would be preceded by a preparatory meeting on May 26 in Rome.

The statement was issued after a meeting of senior officials from countries in the U.N.-backed force which Italy is leading after the failure of dubious savings schemes swept Albania towards anarchy in March. Italy also welcomed a decision by Portugal to join the force.

Franz Vranitzky, an envoy of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe, was to fly back to Tirana on Thursday for his second visit in a week in a bid to head off the prospect of more turmoil over planned elections.

Wednesday's meeting, attended by Albanian undersecretary for foreign affairs Pavli Zeri, called on all Albanian political forces to "abstain from any initiative that could complicate the situation and to cooperate with the special envoy".

President Sali Berisha has said he will call new elections on June 29 but most political parties threatened to boycott the vote after Berisha's rightist Democratic Party pushed through an election law which other parties said was biased in its favour.
